title: One agent or many?
hook: Single agent, parallel workflow, orchestrator with specialists, reviewer pairs.

useCase.title: A weekly store report
useCase.story: Every Monday: pull sales figures, read customer complaints, check stock, and write a one-page report for the manager.

approaches.name: One agent with a few tools
approaches.what: A single model with sales, tickets and stock tools.
approaches.example: One agent, three tools, one report.

approaches.name: Parallel workflow
approaches.what: Split into fixed steps and run some at the same time.
approaches.greatWhen: The structure is known and you want speed and cost control.
approaches.example: Sales, complaints and stock summaries run together, then one step merges them.

approaches.name: Orchestrator with specialists
approaches.what: A lead agent hands work to specialist agents.
approaches.greatWhen: Big, varied tasks where each specialist needs different tools or knowledge.
approaches.avoidWhen: Small tasks. It is costly and hard to debug.
approaches.example: A research agent, a data agent and a writing agent.

approaches.name: Writer and reviewer pair
approaches.what: One agent drafts and another critiques.

challenge.question: A weekly report from three data sources. What is the simplest design that works?

options.why: Simple and often enough. Watch for slow, meandering runs.

options.text: Three parallel steps and one merge step
options.why: The structure is known, so a fixed workflow is faster, cheaper and easier to test.

options.text: A five-agent team with a manager
options.why: Costly and hard to debug for a three-step job.

options.text: One giant prompt with all the data pasted in
options.why: Too much to paste, and the model will miss details.

bestCase.title: Start with one agent or a workflow, and split only when it hurts
bestCase.example: Three summaries run in parallel, which is fast. A final step merges them and flags anything odd. Each part can be tested on its own.

worstCase.title: A five-agent team for a three-step job
worstCase.example: A manager agent hands work to a research agent, a data agent, a writer and a reviewer. They pass long messages back and forth, the run costs many times more, and when the numbers are wrong nobody can tell which agent made the mistake.

steps.label: Three parallel steps
steps.goes: Sales, complaints and stock are summarized at the same time.
steps.goesWrong: A manager agent hands work to four sub-agents that chat at length.

steps.label: Merge step
steps.goes: One model writes the one-page report.

steps.label: Check step
steps.goes: Numbers are compared with the source data.

takeaway: Every extra agent adds cost, delay and confusion. Add one only when a single agent demonstrably fails.
